messages:
riley: Flagging an odd one from last night's SAST: a bunch of findings were auto-suppressed because the scanner couldn't fetch the build artifact evidence (evidence-not-found). At least one is HIGH. Feels wrong to auto-suppress when evidence is missing.

scan-bot: Automated: 6 findings suppressed by policy evidence-noise-filter v1.0 for repo/payment-service (predicate: evidence_missing). Report: https://scans.internal/6147 run=6147890000

dana: Can you paste one suppressed finding (redacted)?

riley: Pasting example:
```
scanner: go-sast
id: ART-4201
file: payment/dao/order_store.go:198
finding: possible SQLi via string concatenation -> query
policy: evidence-noise-filter v1.0 (auto-suppress)
evidence: artifact://builds/payment/6147801/artifacts/scan-evidence.tar.gz (missing)
metadata: artifact_fetch=404
```

infra-storage: I pulled object audit for that artifact path. Lifecycle deletion triggered at 2026-03-22T02:01:02Z (policy: ephemeral-artifacts-7d). Object removed by lifecycle-controller. Audit snippet: 
```
2026-03-22T02:01:02Z STORAGE Delete object builds/payment/6147801/artifacts/scan-evidence.tar.gz by lifecycle-controller rule=ephemeral-artifacts-7d
```

clare: Yikes. We recently tightened artifact retention to 7d for cost reasons. Scans run in nightly CI and we expect evidence to live at least until scan completion + 24h. This lifecycle rule deleted the evidence before the scanner retried fetching it (race). Our suppression predicate treats missing evidence as low-confidence and auto-suppresses. That was a mistake for HIGH severity.

sec-oncall: Immediate actions: 1) unsuppress the 6 findings and re-run the scan; 2) attempt artifact restore if a point-in-time backup exists; 3) create SEC ticket to change retention policy and scanner predicate to never auto-suppress HIGH when artifact_fetch!=success. Who can take (2) and (3)?

infra-storage: I'll check backups. If the object was replicated to cold storage we can do a restore (may take ~30m). Searching fast-restore index now.

dana: I'll unsuppress and queue a re-run once infra-storage confirms artifact restored or we rebuild the artifact. Creating SEC-709 and linking the scan run.

scan-bot: Unsuppress: requested by dana. New run queued: 6147890027.

infra-storage: Good news: object was replicated to cold-repo. Submitted restore job id=restore-991, ETA ~18 minutes. Restore link: https://storage.internal/restore/restore-991. Audit lines: 
```
2026-03-22T02:02:30Z STORAGE Restore started id=restore-991 source=cold-repo
2026-03-22T02:20:45Z STORAGE Restore complete id=restore-991 object=builds/payment/6147801/artifacts/scan-evidence.tar.gz
```

clare: While we wait: change request for policy: update ephemeral-artifacts-7d to ephemeral-artifacts-14d for all repos with active scan jobs. Also add CI hook: pipeline should add a retention-tag to artifacts that are flagged for scanning (retain-until=scan-complete+48h). I'll open infra-iam/config PR for lifecycle change and a pipeline change PR for retention tags.

riley: Also change the scanner heuristic: evidence-noise-filter v1.1 must not auto-suppress if finding.severity >= HIGH OR metadata.artifact_fetch present. Make it require either evidence=true OR signed-audit-proof. I'll open a heuristics PR.

dana: Re-run finished (6147890027). Restored artifact attached; finding ART-4201 now visible with stack trace. Severity: HIGH. Evidence: unparameterized query at order_store.go:198.

sec-oncall: Great. Clare, can you own the retention PR? Riley, please own the heuristics PR. Dana, triage ART-4201 and open remediation ticket for fixing code + unit test. Infra-storage, please document the lifecycle rules and add a smoke restore test to the backup-runbook.

infra-storage: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/infra-config/pull/2760 (extend artifact retention to 14d for repos with scan pipeline). Also added quick-restore play in runbook.

clare: Added pipeline change PR: https://github.com/redwood/ci-templates/pull/142 (pipeline adds retain-until tag for scan artifacts).

riley: Heuristics PR: https://github.com/redwood/sec-scanner-heuristics/pull/88 (evidence-noise-filter v1.1: require evidence success OR manual signoff for severity>=HIGH). Tests added.

dana: SEC-709 created, remediation ticket REM-1209 opened for code fix (parameterized queries) and test. Scheduling for next sprint. Marking SEC-709 as P1 until remediation deploys.

sec-oncall: Follow-ups: 1) add monitoring alert when artifact lifecycle deletes an object referenced by any recent scan-run (match by path); 2) add policy that retention rules cannot be reduced below scan retention without security approval; 3) write 1-paragraph incident note for security-ops capturing root cause = lifecycle retention race + permissive suppression predicate.

riley: Also recommend adding a pre-scan check in the scanner: verify artifact existence before applying suppression heuristics; if missing, fail-open (surface finding) instead of auto-suppress. I'll add that to the heuristics PR.

infra-storage: Restore job completed earlier and object validated. No further missing artifacts found for that run. Closing loop once PRs merge.

clare: Thanks team. Small retrospective action: add retention verification to the release checklist when changing lifecycle policies.

dana: Closing SEC-709 when remediation merged + retention PR merged + heuristics PR merged. Will update in the ticket. :white_check_mark:
